newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia zinc miners seen suppliers to KZ smelter.
newsitem.headline: Australia zinc miners seen suppliers to KZ smelter.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd and other Australian miners are potential suppliers of zinc concentrates to a new smelter planned for Townsville, Queensland.
But the owner, Korea Zinc Co Ltd, is keeping its supply options open, a smelter official said on Wednesday.

Korea Zinc is also considering mines outside of Australia to supply concentrates once the smelter starts up in about two-and-a-half years, said Michael Kennedy, a director of Korea Zinc subsidiary Sun Metals.
Sun Metals is constructing the smelter.
Construction work on the A$530 million first stage of the smelter with a capacity of 170,000 tonnes a year began July 1, with the official ground-breaking ceremony scheduled for July 30.
Australia's vast reserves of zinc strongly suggests local mines will be getting some of the business, although at this stage MIM and Korea Zinc are only in discussions, Kennedy said.
But given MIM's long-running supply arrangements into the Korean zinc market, it is seen as a frontrunner, a source close the project said.
"It's fairly likely Mount Isa Mines concentrate will find its way into Korea Zinc's new smelter," he told Reuters.
An MIM spokesman confirmed MIM was in talks with Korea Zinc over supplying material to the smelter.
But details were confidential, given sensitive market conditions, the spokesman said.
Korea Zinc already buys about 45,000 tonnes of concentrates from Mount Isa to feed its smelter in Onsan, South Korea.
However, the Mount Isa lode will exhaust its reserves in the next few years.

But an extension of the arrangement between the two companies raises the prospect that MIM's proposed A$250 million George Fisher zinc mine will proceed, eventually supplying both smelters, sources close to the project believe.
MIM expects to complete a study into the feasibility of developing George Fisher early next year.
George Fisher is an 80 million tonne resource grading 12 percent zinc, located 22 km from Mount Isa.
The first stage of the Korea Zinc smelter is due to be completed by late in 1999.

The location of the smelter, near Townsville's port, meant the company could import concentrate from other mines in the Asia-Pacific region, such as Cominco Ltd's Red Dog mine in Alaska, Kennedy said.
"Relatively speaking, we'd be quite a competitive receiver of that material (from Red Dog)," Kennedy said.
"A lot of it right now goes to Europe. It's going to be US$10 (a tonne) cheaper to come down to Townsville," he said.
The yet-to-be-finalised Century Zinc project, also in Queensland, is another potential supplier, although it faces a number of hurdles stemming from Aboriginal land claims.
In addition, Century may encounter less competitive freight rates to Townsville.

Also, about half of the Century's concentrate output of 780,000 tonnes under the current blueprint has been earmarked for shipment to the Budelco smelter in Holland, owned by Pasminco Ltd, which plans to buy Century from Rio Tinto Ltd
Century could also become a supplier to Pasminco's Risdon smelter, located in Tasmania, Pasminco has said.
A number of smaller zinc mines in Australia could also supply the smelter, such as RGC Ltd's Thalanga mine and The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's Cannington mine.
Concentrates from the McArthur River mine operated by MIM is seen as a less likely candidate given the bulk nature of the material it produces, Kennedy said.
A second stage of the smelter, duplicating the first, was tentatively planned for completion by about 2004, Kennedy said.
The second stage would also cost around A$500 million and would double production capacity to 340,000 tonnes.
